item.title: Allow writing of files in docker in Linux
item.description:
I have been working on a small project in Python: functainer. The goal of this project is to provide a Python package to run functions in docker seamlessly: you only will docker and Python to run it.

Anyway, that project uses files as a mean of communication, i.e. there is a file volume that the container uses to write the output, and make it reachable by the host.

When the host is a Linux machine, docker daemon runs on root user, and that user is not the same than yours (obviously). A way to avoid having a Permission Denied error is to run your container with your user y making use of –user parameter in the docker container run command, e.g.:
